fixtures: Built by the sibling build_fixtures*.py scripts. Each era gets its own fixture tree ('old' = pre-v5.0.0 layout, 'new' = current layout) so a skill is graded inside its own generation's world rather than against another generation's file layout.
comparison: Valid skill-effect comparisons are within a single era only: old/skill vs old/without, or new/skill vs new/without. Never compare old/without against new/without -- both lack the skill, so any difference between them says nothing about the skill.

evals.prompt: notification-badge 関連ドキュメント(PRD/spec/adr)の整合性をチェックしてください。
evals.expected_output: A severity-classified report of two real, PRD/spec/adr-scoped defects -- spec's FR-003 (clear_badge) claims traceability to PRD's FR_002, whose text never mentions clearing; and spec's constraint section (99+ threshold) contradicts a later decision-log entry that changed the threshold to 101+ -- with no invented findings, no spec-vs-code comparison (out of this skill's documented scope; that's check-spec's job), and no proposal to auto-rewrite the PRD from downstream.
files: Fixture carries two deliberate, era-independent, PRD/spec/adr-scoped defects for the checker to find: (1) spec's FR-003 cites PRD's FR_002 as its source, but FR_002's text only covers badge display/cap, never clearing -- an unjustified traceability claim; (2) the decision log (built per era: adr/{feature}.md for new, appended into *_design.md for old) contains a later entry that changed the '99+' cap threshold to 101+, which spec's own constraint section still contradicts. Both are detectable from document text alone, unlike the project's earlier fixture design which conflated this skill's scope with check-spec's (spec-vs-code) scope. Built per era by build_fixtures.py.
